question: A finite sequence of numbers $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is said to be alternating if $a_1>a_2,a_2<a_3,a_3>a_4,a_4<a_5,\ldots$, or $a_1<a_2,a_2>a_3,a_3<a_4,a_4>a_5,\ldots$. How many alternating sequences of length $5$, with distinct numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_5$ can be formed such that $a_i\in\{1,2,\ldots,20\}$ for $i=1,\ldots,5$?
